sources.title: US Justice Department reassigns about a dozen civil rights attorneys amid shakeup

supported_event_claim: Reuters reported that DOJ was reassigning about a dozen senior career Civil Rights Division attorneys, while at least nine other attorneys were affected by reassignments or resignations; some were moved to FOIA or internal discrimination-complaint work. The report also says the division was directed to investigate companies suspected of favoring foreign visa workers over U.S. workers. This supports personnel departures/reassignments and a shift toward certain discrimination investigations, but does not establish that all departures were quits or that attorneys were personally targeted for 'rev
reason: Direct contemporaneous Reuters reporting supports the narrower, verified personnel shakeup and policy shift; the more sweeping characterization in the row is not fully supported as fact.

sources.title: Pentagon directs military to pull library books that address diversity, anti-racism, gender issues

supported_event_claim: AP reported that the Pentagon ordered military leaders and commands to pull and review library books addressing diversity, anti-racism or gender issues, initially sequestering materials identified as incompatible with the department's mission. AP separately reported that the Education Department's Office for Civil Rights dismissed 11 complaints alleging that book restrictions created a hostile environment for children and rescinded guidance treating such book bans as civil-rights violations.
reason: Both components are directly supported by contemporaneous AP reports. The sources describe military libraries/commands and OCR complaints; they do not warrant broader claims that every Pentagon school quarantined books.

sources.title: What's in the tax and spending bill that Trump has signed into law

supported_event_claim: AP reported that President Trump signed the tax-and-spending bill into law on July 4, 2025; it imposed new work requirements for many Medicaid recipients and included a one-year bar on Medicaid payments to family-planning providers that provide abortions, namely Planned Parenthood. This is a final enacted provision, not merely a proposal.
reason: The AP page directly verifies enactment and the Medicaid/Planned Parenthood provision. It does not by itself establish the row's precise healthcare-loss estimate, so that exaggeration is not repeated.

sources.title: Relatives of missing Venezuelan migrants desperate for answers after US deportations to El Salvador

supported_event_claim: Reuters reported that after President Trump invoked the 1798 Alien Enemies Act on March 15, 2025, the administration deported 137 Venezuelans to El Salvador even as a judge ordered removals halted; relatives struggled to obtain information and some suspected their family members were among those sent to the prison. Reuters also reported that the administration provided few details about identities. The 'missing' characterization is reported relatives' inability to locate or obtain information about people, not proof that people disappeared or that all removals were unlawful.
reason: The contemporaneous Reuters report directly verifies the invocation, March deportations and relatives' reported lack of information, while distinguishing allegations/suspicions from established facts.

sources.title: Medicaid was signed into law 60 years ago. Trump's big bill is chiseling it back

supported_event_claim: AP reported that the enacted One Big Beautiful Bill would cut more than $1 trillion over a decade from federal health care and food assistance, largely through Medicaid work requirements and shifting costs to states; it estimated 10 million more people would lack health insurance. AP described Medicaid as serving, among others, disabled people and noted that some older adults and other recipients face new work, education or community-service requirements.
reason: The AP report supports major enacted Medicaid and safety-net reductions and potential coverage losses affecting vulnerable populations. It does not establish a precise $900 billion Medicaid-only figure or that the law will re-institutionalize disabled Americans, so those claims are not stated as facts.

sources.title: Unleashing Alaska's Extraordinary Resource Potential

supported_event_claim: On January 20, 2025, President Trump issued an executive order directing the Interior Secretary to withdraw a prior halt, rescind cancellation of certain Arctic National Wildlife Refuge leases, initiate additional leasing through the Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program, and issue permits needed for exploration, development, and production. The order was a directive to pursue opening ANWR to drilling, not proof that drilling or leasing actually began that day.
reason: The official White House order directly verifies the January 20 action, but the row's wording is stronger than the source: it did not establish that ANWR was already opened for drilling on that date.

sources.title: US EPA cutting workforce by 23%, closing research division

supported_event_claim: On July 18, 2025, the EPA said it was cutting its workforce by at least 23%—from 16,155 employees in January to 12,448—and closing its Office of Research and Development, which had about 1,500 employees. EPA said it would create a new Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions.
reason: Reuters contemporaneously and directly reported all three elements. The workforce figure is an EPA-stated planned/reported reduction, not an independently audited final headcount.

sources.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Modifies Two National Monuments, Restoring Sensible Land Management

supported_event_claim: On July 13, 2026, the White House said President Trump signed a proclamation reducing Bears Ears National Monument from approximately 1.36 million acres to approximately 121,100 acres—about a 91% reduction—and the proclamation reserved approximately 121,096 acres.
reason: The official White House fact sheet and proclamation directly verify the date, action, and acreage. The neutral description is a boundary reduction, rather than the unsupported shorthand that the monument was simply 'shrunk 90%' without specifying the baseline and action.

No acceptable official or Reuters/AP source was found verifying that Clean Water Act wetland protection was stripped on November 17, 2026. The EPA materials located describe a proposed Waters of the United States rule and existing litigation/status information; they do not verify a final action eliminating wetland protection on that date.

sources.title: National Climate Assessment

supported_event_claim: A Congressional Research Service report updated July 2, 2025, stated that the U.S. Global Change Research Program website was inactive on July 2. This supports that the federal climate-assessment program's website was offline by July 2, but does not verify the row's specific June 24 date; June 24 is associated with a separate Climate.gov/NOAA website change, not the National Climate Assessment site.
reason: The federal CRS source directly verifies the site being inactive, but gives July 2, 2025 rather than June 24. The date discrepancy is explicitly preserved rather than presented as confirmed.

sources.title: Congress kills Biden era methane fee on oil, gas producers

supported_event_claim: Congress disapproved and EPA removed the Waste Emissions Charge (the Inflation Reduction Act methane fee) from the Code of Federal Regulations in 2025. The verified sources do not establish an ‘18-month pollution pass’; that characterization is omitted.
reason: The Reuters report verifies congressional repeal, and EPA's official page verifies that the rule is no longer in effect following the congressional resolution. The claimed 18-month pass is not supported by these sources.

No accepted official federal or AP/Reuters page was found that verifies the precise compound claim that the Superfund budget was slashed 47% and that cleanups were halted. A proposed budget reduction, if any, would not by itself establish that cleanups were halted; the claim conflates a proposal with an operational fact.

sources.title: US farm agency lost 20000 staff first five months of Trump administration

supported_event_claim: A Reuters report citing a USDA inspector-general review reported that more than 5,800 employees left the U.S. Forest Service, about 16% of its staff, during the period tracked in 2025.
reason: The source supports a Forest Service staffing loss exceeding 5,000, but the neutral wording ‘left’ is used rather than asserting that all departures were firings.

sources.title: EPA Proposes Repeal of Biden-Harris EPA Regulations for Power Plants, Which, If Finalized, Would Save Americans More than a Billion Dollars a Year

supported_event_claim: On June 11, 2025, EPA proposed repealing the Biden-era greenhouse-gas standards for fossil-fuel power plants and proposed repealing certain 2024 amendments to the power-plant Mercury and Air Toxics Standards. These were proposals at that time, not final actions; ‘weakening mercury limits’ is a characterization rather than the precise regulatory description.
reason: EPA's official release directly verifies the proposal and expressly conditions the consequences on finalization. The claim is narrowed to distinguish proposed repeal from a completed rule change.

sources.title: Bureau of Land Management reopens vast areas of National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska for energy development
sources.publisher: Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Department of the Interior

supported_event_claim: BLM announced on December 22, 2025 that its updated plan reopened nearly 82% of Alaska’s 23-million-acre National Petroleum Reserve to oil-and-gas leasing.
reason: The official BLM page verifies the 82%-of-23-million-acres action, but it dates the action to 2025-12-22. It does not support a future event dated November 13, 2026; that date is corrected rather than treated as verified.

sources.title: Trump administration ends key grant program that helps communities prepare for disasters

supported_event_claim: FEMA announced on April 4, 2025 that it was ending the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) grant program. The source supports cancellation of BRIC, not a claim that FEMA itself was dismantled; it also does not establish that the program was officially called a 'Billion-Dollar Disaster Resilience' program.
reason: Contemporaneous AP reporting directly quotes FEMA's announcement. The wording is narrowed to the verified program cancellation and avoids the unsupported broader claim that FEMA was dismantled.

sources.title: Trump administration announces plan for new oil drilling off the coasts of California and Florida

supported_event_claim: On November 20, 2025, the administration announced a proposed five-year offshore leasing plan that included six potential lease sales along California and proposed drilling/lease sales in the Gulf region at least 100 miles off Florida. This was a proposal, not completed drilling or a final leasing action; the sources do not support changing the event date to November 20, 2026.
reason: Both AP and Reuters contemporaneously report the precise California/Florida proposal and distinguish it from final leasing or actual drilling.

sources.title: EPA Releases Proposal to Rescind Obama-Era Endangerment Finding, Regulations that Paved the Way for Electric Vehicle Mandates

supported_event_claim: On July 29, 2025, EPA announced a proposal to rescind the 2009 greenhouse-gas Endangerment Finding. EPA described that finding as the legal prerequisite for Clean Air Act section 202(a) vehicle greenhouse-gas standards; Reuters reported that rescinding it would remove the legal foundation for U.S. greenhouse-gas regulations. The verified action was a proposal at that time, not a final rescission.
reason: The EPA release directly verifies the proposal and its asserted legal basis, while contemporaneous Reuters reporting confirms the significance and distinguishes the announced action.

sources.title: Trump administration cuts environmental justice programs at EPA, DOJ, sources say

supported_event_claim: On February 6, 2025, EPA confirmed that 168 employees in its Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights had been placed on administrative leave; Reuters also reported staff reductions in similar Justice Department programs. The source supports placing 168 EPA staff on leave, not the stronger claim that the entire environmental-justice program was permanently wiped out.
reason: Reuters directly reports the agency confirmation and gives the precise number. The claim is narrowed because 'wiped out' is not established by the report.

sources.title: Trump administration memo urges countries to reject plastic production caps at UN talks

supported_event_claim: At the start of the August 2025 U.N. plastic-treaty talks, the United States sent letters to at least several countries urging rejection of a global pact containing plastic-production limits and restrictions on some additives/products. The memo set U.S. negotiating red lines and opposed upstream production targets; the source does not establish that the United States sought to 'kill' the entire treaty.
reason: Reuters verified the letters, memo, timing, and substance. The claim is neutralized from 'kill the treaty' to the documented lobbying against production caps and related upstream provisions.

sources.title: Pro-Trump mob storms US Capitol in bid to overturn election

supported_event_claim: On January 6, 2021, a pro-Trump mob stormed and breached the U.S. Capitol, forcing lawmakers into hiding and interrupting the congressional electoral-vote count.
reason: The contemporaneous AP report, published January 6, 2021, directly describes the mob storming the Capitol and the resulting disruption; this verifies the breach event rather than merely discussing the broader political controversy.

sources.title: Facts about the U.S. House probe of the Jan. 6, 2021, assault on the Capitol

supported_event_claim: Reuters reported that four officers later died by suicide and that 140 other officers were injured in connection with the January 6 Capitol attack.
reason: The directly fetched Reuters article states that four officers took their own lives and that 140 others were injured. The source supports the approximately 140-or-more injured-officers figure, while the neutral wording avoids treating the count as an exact immutable total.
